subject: Private cluster throughput & tail-latency surge — exec briefing requested
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@helioshealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health SRE <sre@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop and tail latency on our private cluster

Hi Laura —

We started seeing a spike in 95th/99th latency and a ~30% throughput drop on our private VPC cluster starting ~07:30 PT this morning. Errors are mostly 504 timeouts from the private inference nodes and a few model-decode stalls. Our ingest rate hasn't changed.

Attached is a small sample of request/response traces and a kv-cache dump from one affected node. We believe something changed after the daily maintenance window (00:00-02:00) but haven't identified a root cause.

Can Redwood help triage urgently? This is impacting our triage pipeline for clinician alerts. If you think this needs an executive sync we can make room.

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Head of Platform Engineering — Helios Health
Attachment: helios_perf-0929-sample.json (request/response traces)
Attachment: kvcache-dump-0929.txt (kv cache dump, truncated)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop and tail latency on our private cluster

Sara —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the attachments. I’m escalating internally and we’ll start a live triage. Initial ask: could you share the node IDs for the failing hosts and a short sample of the workload (prompt size distribution)? The kv-cache dump is helpful — we’ll look for cache thrashing/evictions.

I’m looping Marcus (serving runtime lead) and Evelyn (on-call infra) to pick this up. Connor, can you triage the sample and confirm whether the decode stalls correlate with heavy KV cache misses or with autoscaler activity?

Sara — happy to set an exec sync if this remains unresolved after initial triage.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop and tail latency on our private cluster

Quick notes from initial analysis of the sample:
- The traces show a cluster-wide pattern: a small number of requests are experiencing 10-20s decode stalls, others are fine.
- KV cache metrics for the reported node IDs show repeated full-cache evictions correlated with GC cycles in the host JVM process that handles routing. That suggests high concurrency pushing the KV cache eviction threshold.
- Autoscaler logs show multiple scale-in/scale-out oscillations between 07:15-07:40 PT; kube-probe failures were present on 2 nodes.

Hypothesis: a probe flapping event triggered transient pod churn; combined with sudden concurrency spikes for a particular prompt shape, this caused KV cache thrash, leading to expensive cold-decode paths and tail latency.

Immediate remediation we suggest:
1) Pin a read-only cache TTL on the problematic pool to avoid aggressive eviction (short-term).
2) Temporarily increase the target capacity by +25% for Helios private pool to absorb burst.
3) Patch probe behavior to be more lenient for the inference container (increase failureThreshold from 3 -> 6) while we root-cause the flapping.

I’ll implement 1) and 2) if we get approval from Laura/Aditya for the capacity bump; 3) needs a short config rollout window. We should also run a mock load to validate.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop and tail latency on our private cluster

Updating with infra findings:
- The cloud provider reported intermittent network blips in the region from 07:12-07:38 PT impacting health probes to a subset of instances.
- The autoscaler observed the flapping and applied aggressive scale-downs; our default cooldown window was too short for this pattern.

Actions I’m taking now:
- Increase cooldown window from 120s -> 600s for the Helios node pool.
- Temporarily exclude 3 suspect instances from the pool for deeper inspection; the instances will remain in drain rather than terminate.

Evelyn — I agree with Marcus on the cache TTL change. Laura — please confirm if we should apply the +25% capacity bump immediately (we can apply to Dedicated/private capacity config).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Approved for the +25% temporary capacity bump and TTL pin. Marcus and Evelyn — proceed with both. Marcus, coordinate with Connor for the mock load once the scaled capacity is live.

Sara — we’ll apply the fixes now and run a controlled replay against a canary subset of your traffic. If the tail-latency persists after these mitigations we’ll request an exec sync (I’ll escalate to product and infra leadership).

Also request from my side: please upload a 10-minute pcap and the pod-level probe logs to the Drive link in related_links so we can correlate with cloud provider events.

—Laura

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@helioshealth.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation summary and exec ask (if needed)

Status update after remediation window: summary below. Please note this is a working note; we’ll convert to a formal incident postmortem if the issue recurs.

What we changed (09/29):
- Increased private pool capacity +25% for Helios (temporary)
- Pinned KV cache TTL for affected pool to reduce eviction frequency
- Increased kube-probe failureThreshold and expanded autoscaler cooldown window
- Isolated and inspected three suspect instances (no hardware faults found)

Result:
- Throughput recovered to ~98% of baseline within 45 minutes of the capacity bump.
- 95th latency reduced from ~18s -> 420ms for the replayed traffic; a small subset (~0.3%) still sees intermittent 2–3s tail latency which we attribute to degraded cache warmup for very large prompt shapes.

Remaining asks / next steps:
1) Follow-up runbook update: include explicit guidance to increase cooldowns and probe thresholds for private pools in noisy network environments. I’ve attached a draft (runbook_private_perf_v2.pdf).
2) Engineering task: add a light-weight distributed KV cache warmup pass during scale events to reduce cold-decode tail. Marcus to propose scope/estimate.
3) Exec ask: if Helios wants a durable SLA credit or commitment on response timelines for private cluster performance incidents, we should coordinate with Sales Leadership (Aditya) and Legal.

Sara — can you confirm whether Helios is comfortable with the temporary capacity and the proposed follow-ups? If not, I will schedule an executive sync tomorrow to align on SLAs and credit discussion.

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration.

—Laura
Attachment: runbook_private_perf_v2.pdf (draft remediation runbook)
